Subject: Regulatory BCP snapshot and RTO/RPO evidence request for HarborBank SOC2 review

Hi Lauren,

We are compiling the control evidence set for HarborBank's SOC 2 in-scope systems and need a concise snapshot of your Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery posture focused on demonstration artifacts. Specifically we are looking for:

- The latest tabletop or simulation report (date, participants, summary of outcomes)
- Measured RTO and RPO figures for the primary inference path and control plane (typical, p95, and longest observed during tests)
- A short chronology/log of the most recent recovery run (steps performed, duration, any manual interventions)
- Any runbook excerpts that detail failover steps and KV cache warm-up expectations

Can you please provide the above artifacts or point me to a secure link? HarborBank's compliance team would like the materials by end of week to keep the audit timeline. If you need an NDA or file transfer instructions we can accommodate.

Thanks,
Sam Liu
Lead Auditor, Horizon Audit Services
sam.liu@horizonaudit.com

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are the initial artifacts we maintain for audit purposes: a short simulation report (BCP_Simulation_Report_Feb2027.pdf) and a machine-readable RTO/RPO matrix (rto_rpo_matrix.csv). High-level notes:

- Most recent tabletop: 2027-02-18 (cross-functional: infra, runtime, product, security). See report and the recovery log.
- Measured RTO (inference path): typical cold-start-to-scaling recovery 3m 20s, p95 5m 10s during the simulation that included a partial region outage.
- Measured RPO: client-visible state is zero for request data (no persistent request store); model state recovery (KV cache) achieves steady state for common prefixes at p95 ~48s across regions during warm-up phase. See rto_rpo_matrix.csv for breakdown by cluster and model family.
- Control plane recovery (auth/management): p95 under 4m, fastest 1m 40s (we maintain a separate runbook).

Grace has volunteered to add the technical runbook excerpts and the raw recovery run log into the shared Drive link below. I am also attaching a blank attestation template we typically ask customers to sign for acceptance.

Attachments: BCP_Simulation_Report_Feb2027.pdf, rto_rpo_matrix.csv, attestation_template.docx

Next steps:
- Grace will drop the recovery_run_2027-02-18.log and a small runbook excerpt into the Drive folder by EOD.
- If you need additional detail on warm cache metrics (per-model prefix distribution) we can extract sample queries.

Let me know if HarborBank needs the artifacts delivered via a secured SFTP or a signed DocuSign attestation.

Best,

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>

Hi Sam / Lauren —

Following Lauren's note, a few tactical artifacts attached here and a short technical summary inline. I dropped the raw run log and a runbook excerpt into the Drive folder (link included in the thread metadata): recovery_run_2027-02-18.log and runbook_excerpt.md.

Technical summary (short):
- Trigger: simulated us-west region network partition (tabletop + controlled failover).
- Primary action: routing policy switched traffic to us-east with auto-fallback for requests pinned to dedicated capacity.
- Inference path recovery sequence (trimmed):
  1) Health checks detect degraded GPU nodes (0s)
  2) Autoscaler tears down affected worker pools and starts warm pools in us-east (12s–90s var)
  3) KV cache prefill kicks off for high-frequency prefixes using persistent snapshot + prioritized replay (avg prefill time for top 50 prefixes: 32s)
  4) Traffic ramp to steady state (additional 1m–3m depending on model concurrency)

Observed timings from the 2027-02-18 run (attached log):
- Time to first successful inference in failover path: 1m 55s
- Time to reach 95% of baseline throughput: 4m 50s
- KV cache top-50 prefix steady-state (p95): 48s

Notes on methodology: we run combined automated and manual steps for tabletop exercises to validate orchestration, and we record timestamps at each handoff. The raw log contains the event IDs and timestamps you can reference for Azure/GCP trace correlation.

If you'd like a matrix of per-model warm-up traces (sampled), say which model families and we'll provide CSV extracts.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com
